sections.h2: Which Allen County, KY offices handle my tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work in Allen County. The Property Valuation Administrator decides what each parcel is worth. The Allen County Sheriff then collects what is owed. The PVA neither sets your tax nor takes payment: the bill comes from the assessed value times rates adopted by the county government, the school board and special districts such as the library and health department.

  • PVA: 201 W Main St #1, Scottsville, KY 42164, phone (270) 237-3711, weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon.
  • Sheriff, who collects: 194 W Wood St, Scottsville, KY 42164, phone (270) 237-3210, with a tax bill search on the sheriff's county web page.
  • An owner who never received a bill can reach the Sheriff's Office at 270-237-3388, the number the PVA's page lists for that.

State law picks January 1 as the day property is valued and also as the day ownership is fixed for tax purposes. A house bought later in the year is billed to the prior owner for that year, though the PVA tries to mail the new owner a copy based on the recorded deed. The PVA's county web page says the certified tax roll and ownership information are posted online for anyone to check.

sections.h2: How much extra does an unpaid Allen County tax bill cost?
sections.html:
Costs rise in stages once the sheriff passes a bill to the county clerk. The Revenue Department shows a $1,000 bill becoming a $1,254.00 certificate of delinquency after a 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add-on fee and an assumed 4 percent commission. Monthly interest of 1 percent follows, along with commissions for the clerk and the county attorney.

State example of a $1,000 bill after transfer to the county clerk (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
When paidTotal due
Within five business days of transfer$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
In May, second month of interest$1,627.61
After newspaper advertising in June$1,659.90
At the tax sale, paid by a third-party purchaser$1,704.21

These figures rest on assumed rates, and a real bill uses the sheriff's actual commission. Request a written payoff from the Allen County Sheriff ahead of closing so the title company works from a firm number.

sections.h2: What are the tax payment windows in Allen County?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets the calendar. A bill paid in full on or before November 1 is reduced by 2 percent. The printed amount applies through December, January brings a 5 percent penalty, and from February the penalty is 10 percent.

The sheriff keeps collecting until April 15. When business closes that day, unpaid bills go to the county clerk, a lien is recorded on each parcel, and the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency. A sale cannot happen sooner than 90 days later and must be held within 135. Between those dates the county attorney mails notices, and the clerk publishes the list 30 to 45 days ahead of the sale.

The lien from an overdue bill travels with the land. KRS 134.015(5) keeps it alive until payment or until the 11-year limit in KRS 134.420 passes, whoever holds title. A buyer inherits the problem, so a seller with a balance should pay it off or arrange for it to be paid from the sale.

sections.h2: How do I contest an Allen County assessment?
sections.html:
Go to the PVA first, since the state demands a conference with the PVA or a deputy before an appeal can be filed. The real property roll sits open for public viewing for 13 days from the first Monday in May, with dates advertised by the PVA in the paper of widest circulation.

After that meeting, the appeal goes to the county clerk, due by the end of the next workday after viewing ends. A board of local property owners hears it 25 to 35 days after viewing ends. Bring condition photos, repair estimates, insurance records and nearby sales. Evidence counts only if it is presented with you and the PVA's representative both present, and any change in value needs a written explanation.

You may make an audio recording of the hearing. When bills print before a decision, your own stated value is used, and a supplemental bill follows if the board finds a higher one.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Kentucky homestead exemption in Allen County?
sections.html:
Owners at least 65 years old, and owners with a total disability classification, can claim it. It is worth $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years and is subtracted from assessed value before rates apply. A house worth $192,300, the Census midpoint for Allen County, would be taxed on $143,200.

Send the application to the Allen County PVA, (270) 237-3711. Disability claims are renewed every year except for veterans with a service-connected disability and owners found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What should I know about Allen County, Kentucky, before selling?
sections.html:
Allen County touches Tennessee and was carved out in 1815 from Barren and Warren counties. Scottsville is the seat and the only city. The Bowling Green metropolitan area includes the county, and bordering it are Warren, Barren, Monroe and Simpson counties in Kentucky plus Macon and Sumner counties in Tennessee. A fire at the courthouse in 1902 destroyed some county records, which can make very old title research harder. The county covers 344 square miles of land, and 77.5 percent of residents live in rural areas.

The population has been climbing. The 2020 census counted 20,588 residents and the latest federal estimate, for July 2025, is 22,536, a rise of 9.5 percent.

  • Housing units: 9,390 as of 2025.
  • Owner-occupied share: 74.5 percent.
  • Midpoint home value: $192,300.
  • Midpoint household income: $61,403, with 14.3 percent of people below the poverty line.
  • Mean commute: 27.3 minutes, against 23.8 minutes in neighboring Adair County.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 17.

The county counted 8,035 households of 2.63 people on average, and 90.9 percent of people had not moved in the previous twelve months. The sheriff's office does more than collect: its county web page also lists enforcement of foreclosures, repossessions and tax delinquencies among its duties. Median monthly owner costs run $1,231 with a mortgage and $424 without one, and median gross rent is $844.

With only 17 permits in a county of more than 9,000 housing units, most sales are of existing houses. A seller who has the tax account paid up and a clean deed of record faces fewer questions at closing.

faqs.q: Which Allen County office takes tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff does, as KRS 134.140 and 160.500 provide. The office at 194 W Wood St in Scottsville answers at (270) 237-3210. The PVA's role ends with valuation.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Allen County taxes late?
faqs.a: A 5 percent penalty applies in January and 10 percent after that, added to the printed amount. Once the bill reaches the clerk after April 15, monthly interest of 1 percent, commissions and fees join in, as the state's worked examples show.

faqs.q: Is the Allen County homestead exemption automatic at age 65?
faqs.a: No, you have to apply at the Allen County PVA. The amount is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, set by the Kentucky Department of Revenue. Qualifying owners must be 65 or over, or totally disabled.

faqs.q: I bought a house in Allen County after January 1. Who gets the tax bill?
faqs.a: The seller's name appears on that year's bill, since ownership for tax purposes is fixed as of January 1. The PVA attempts to mail a copy to the buyer. If nothing comes, call the sheriff.

faqs.q: Can an Allen County tax lien block a sale?
faqs.a: It can slow one down. The lien remains on the parcel until it is paid or the 11-year limit under KRS 134.420 passes, regardless of who owns it. Obtain a payoff from the sheriff and clear it at or before closing.
